instruction: Display the URL from the latest Bills email by opening it in a Google Chrome tab.

metadata.explanation: Variation 8: Uses 'display' action and 'Google Chrome' full name. Task displays the first link (https://www.amazon.com/) from the latest Bills email by opening it in Google Chrome. Evaluator verifies all three tabs are present including the new amazon.com tab.

llm_judge_reasons: Semantic mismatch: instruction asks to 'display the URL from the latest Bills email' (singular task: open ONE URL from email), but evaluator checks for exactly 3 specific tabs including 2 pre-existing tabs
Incomplete coverage: the evaluator verifies pre-task state (apple.com, scholar.google.com) rather than focusing on task completion (amazon.com URL opened)
False negative risk: if agent closes pre-existing tabs during task execution, evaluation would fail even though the core task (opening the Bills email URL) was completed correctly

Overly strict verification: evaluator uses are_lists_equal which likely requires exact match of all tabs, making evaluation brittle to agent behavior that doesn't affect task completion (e.g., closing unrelated tabs, tab ordering)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change evaluator to verify only that amazon.com URL is present in open tabs, rather than checking for exact set of 3 specific URLs
Use a metric that checks 'contains expected URL' rather than 'exact list match' - e.g., iterate through open_tabs and check if any tab URL matches amazon.com
Alternative: update instruction to explicitly state 'open the Bills email URL while keeping existing tabs open' to match current evaluator behavior
Consider using a partial match metric that verifies the task-critical URL (amazon.com) is present without requiring specific pre-existing tabs
